register.name: Sovereign sukuk, first issue
register.detail: Subscription opened 27 January 2026 · Public Treasury · Ijara usufruct sukuk · More than 80% subscribed by 12 April 2026, according to the Minister of Finance
register.note: The first sovereign sukuk issue in Algeria; the amount is the sum sought
register.text: The Public Treasury’s first issue of sovereign sukuk, opened to subscription on 27 January 2026 to raise 296.65 billion dinars for large public projects in infrastructure, equipment and public services. On 12 April 2026 the Minister of Finance said more than 80% had been subscribed. It draws on national savings to build public infrastructure, which serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Laghouat–Ghardaïa–El Meniaa railway, second phase
register.detail: Approved, announced 14 July 2026 · Ghardaïa–El Meniaa section, 230 km · Implemented by the Ministry of Public Works and Basic Infrastructure
register.note: Second phase of the 495-kilometre line; the release does not state the instrument
register.text: Financing approved by the Board of Directors of the African Development Bank Group for the 230-kilometre Ghardaïa–El Meniaa section of the line, with integrated infrastructure, institutional support and training for young people and women in railway, logistics, tourism and handicraft trades. The AfDB presents it as part of Algeria’s diversification beyond hydrocarbons; it serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Laghouat–Ghardaïa–El Menéa railway, first phase
register.detail: Approved, announced 12 December 2025 · Loan · Priority sections of the 495 km line and modern railway equipment
register.note: First phase of the 495-kilometre line
register.text: A loan from the African Development Bank for the first phase of the 495-kilometre line: construction of priority sections, modern railway equipment, economic and social platforms for young people, women and local stakeholders, and preparation of a future extension of the network. The AfDB expects it to reshape economic dynamics in southern Algeria over the long term; it serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Hassi Bir Rekaiz field, processing unit contract
register.detail: Signed 5 May 2026 · EPC contract · Sonatrach–PTTEP association with Petrojet and Arkad JSC · New crude oil processing unit, 31,500 barrels a day
register.note: Sonatrach does not state the contract value
register.text: An engineering, procurement and construction contract signed by the Sonatrach–PTTEP association with a consortium of Egypt’s Petrojet and Italy’s Arkad JSC, for a new crude oil processing unit of 31,500 barrels a day at the Hassi Bir Rekaiz field. Sonatrach says this phase will raise production capacity and improve treatment efficiency.

register.name: Illizi South hydrocarbon development
register.detail: Signed 13 October 2025 · Production-sharing contract · 30 years, extendable by 10 · Funded 100% by Midad Energy North Africa
register.note: US$288 million allocated to research investments
register.text: A production-sharing contract between the state energy company and Saudi Arabia’s Midad Energy North Africa for the exploration and exploitation of the Illizi South perimeter, with an investment of around US$5.4 billion funded entirely by the partner. Sonatrach estimates output over the contract at 993 million barrels of oil equivalent, including 125 billion cubic metres of gas.

register.name: Shoreline facility for the Hassi Bir Rekaiz development
register.detail: Approved June 2026 · Dual tranche · $110 million contract finance and $90 million revolving · For Shoreline and Arkad on Phase 2a of the Hassi Bir Rekaiz field
register.note: Supports the Nigerian and Italian contractors on the field’s new processing facility
register.text: A facility from the African Export-Import Bank for Shoreline Power Company and its partners in the Phase 2a development of the Hassi Bir Rekaiz oil field, run by Sonatrach, PTTEP and CEPSA. It finances the contractors rather than the state; the oil revenue it helps raise funds the budget that pays for the seven standards.

register.name: Baladna Algeria, second package of contracts
register.detail: Signed 23 April 2026 · Algiers · Implementation contracts with Algerian and international partners · Powdered milk project in Adrar
register.note: Second phase of a $3.5 billion integrated dairy and powdered milk project
register.text: Contracts for the second phase of the dairy and powdered milk complex built by Baladna Algeria, a company owned 51% by Qatar’s Baladna and 49% by Algeria’s National Investment Fund. The signing came with an airlift of 30,000 dairy cows; it serves the food standard.

register.name: Baladna Algeria, first-phase contracts
register.detail: Signed 28 July 2025 · 14 contracts · Agricultural technology, dairy production lines, irrigation pivots, land preparation and two farms
register.note: More than $500 million; first phase of the $3.5 billion project
register.text: The first package of contracts for the integrated agri-industrial project in Adrar, which aims to meet half of Algeria’s demand for powdered milk and create more than 5,000 jobs. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Integrated phosphate project, phase 1 EPC contracts
register.detail: Signed 12 August 2026 · Algiers · Sonatrach and the Algerian Fertilizers Company with Saipem (processing at Bled El Hadba and Oued El Keberit) and CHEC (port facilities at Annaba)
register.note: No combined value published; Saipem states €500 million for its limited notice to proceed
register.text: Two engineering, procurement and construction contracts for the first phase of the integrated phosphate project, from the mine at Bled El Hadba in Tébessa to the port of Annaba, with an extraction and enrichment capacity of 5.5 million tonnes a year. Fertiliser made at home serves the food standard and the work serves livelihood.

register.name: Gara Djebilet–Tindouf–Béchar railway
register.detail: Inaugurated 1 February 2026 · About 950 km · Financed by the Algerian state, partly built by a Chinese consortium
register.note: No construction cost published
register.text: A heavy-haul mining line that carries iron ore from the Gara Djebilet deposit to Béchar and on to a steel plant near Oran. It opens the south-west to industry and serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Three seawater desalination plants, Tlemcen, Chlef and Mostaganem
register.detail: Signed 29 December 2025 · Three construction contracts · 300,000 cubic metres a day each
register.note: Contract values not published; reported as a programme of about $1 billion
register.text: The first contracts of the additional national desalination programme, signed by Sonatrach with Algerian builders, for three plants of 300,000 cubic metres a day in the north-west. They serve the water standard.

register.name: Five large seawater desalination plants
register.detail: Completed 2025 · Cap Blanc (Oran) opened February 2025; Fouka 2, Koudiat Draouch, Cap Djinet 2 and Tighremt at full capacity July to December 2025 · 300,000 cubic metres a day each
register.note: Programme cost stated by the Algerian authorities, about $2.4 billion
register.text: Five plants in Oran, Tipaza, El Tarf, Boumerdès and Béjaïa, each producing 300,000 cubic metres of drinking water a day, built under Sonatrach. The authorities expect desalination to rise from 18% to 40% of the national water supply; they serve the water standard.

register.name: Algeria Bid Round 2024, five contracts
register.detail: Signed 21 July 2025 · Five production-sharing contracts · 30 years, with 7 years of exploration · Partners include TotalEnergies and QatarEnergy (Ahara), Eni and PTTEP (Reggane II)
register.note: Minimum exploration investment across the five contracts
register.text: The first contracts from Algeria’s first bid round since 2014, under hydrocarbons law 19-13, signed by Sonatrach, ALNAFT and international companies. The partners bear the exploration spending; the revenue funds the public budget.

register.name: Zemoul El Kbar production-sharing contract
register.detail: Signed 7 July 2025 · 30 years, extendable by 10 · 7-year research period · Berkine basin
register.note: Planned exploration and development investment; $110 million for research
register.text: A contract between Sonatrach and Italy’s Eni for the Zemoul El Kbar perimeter, with a separate agreement to market dry gas for export. The partner’s investment raises output whose revenue funds the public budget.

register.name: Hassi Berkane North production-sharing contract
register.detail: Signed 25 February 2025 · Sinopec · Perimeter between Ouargla and El Meniaa, 80 km from Hassi Messaoud
register.note: Projected overall investment for exploration and production
register.text: A contract with China’s Sinopec for the exploration and development of the Hassi Berkane North perimeter, following a head of agreement of March 2024. The partner’s investment raises output whose revenue funds the public budget.

register.name: Letter of credit confirmation facility for Crédit Populaire d’Algérie
register.detail: Signed May 2025 · Algiers, IsDB Group Annual Meetings · Syndicated facility
register.note: Trade finance for public and private clients of the bank
register.text: A syndicated letter of credit confirmation facility from the International Islamic Trade Finance Corporation to Crédit Populaire d’Algérie, a state bank, to support trade transactions and small firms. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: IsDB Group cooperation framework 2025–2027
register.detail: Signed 20 May 2025 · Algiers · Three-year framework · Railways, infrastructure, health and renewable energy
register.note: Over $3 billion over three years, as reported; the IsDB page states no amount
register.text: A cooperation framework between Algeria and the Islamic Development Bank Group for development financing over three years. No Board approval for an Algerian operation under it has been found yet.

register.name: Sahrawi Refugees Response Plan 2024–2025
register.detail: Plan 2024–2025 · UNHCR and 28 partners · Camps near Tindouf
register.note: Requirement for 2025
register.text: The joint plan for the Sahrawi refugees in the camps near Tindouf, covering food, water, shelter, health and education; 81% of the refugees depend on aid. It serves the food, water, shelter, education and health standards.

register.name: EU humanitarian aid to Sahrawi refugees, 2025
register.detail: Committed 2025 · Humanitarian funding · Including sustained funding for WFP food assistance
register.note: EU humanitarian funding in Algeria in 2025
register.text: Funding from the European Union for the Sahrawi refugees in Algeria, including food assistance from the World Food Programme to more than 133,000 people. It serves the food standard.

register.name: 3,000 MW solar photovoltaic programme
register.detail: Signed 14 March 2024 · Sonelgaz · 19 contracts for 20 plants from a 2 GW and a 1 GW tender · Plants of 50 MW to 300 MW
register.note: Contract values not published
register.text: Contracts signed by Sonelgaz, the state utility, with Algerian, joint and foreign companies to build 3,000 MW of solar plants across the country. They serve the energy standard by adding clean power to a grid that is mostly gas-fired.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Reserves
items.label: Gross official reserves, 2025
items.text: A national cushion few nations hold, enough to anchor long-term finance at home.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2024
items.text: Africa’s largest territory: desert sun, gas fields and a Mediterranean coast.

items.name: The Ground
items.label: Of GDP from natural resource rents, 2021
items.text: Oil and gas rents carry the budget; the task is to turn them into assets that outlast them.
items.alt: Gas field installations and pipelines in the Sahara, Algeria

items.name: The Grid
items.label: Of citizens with electricity, 2024
items.text: Every household connected, and every kitchen cooking with clean fuels: a base for industry beyond hydrocarbons.
items.alt: Solar park with power lines on the high plateaus of Algeria

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 29.9% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.
items.alt: Street of white arcaded buildings in central Algiers, Algeria

items.name: Cevital Agro-Industrie
items.text: The food arm of the Cevital group runs, in the port of Béjaïa, what it calls the world’s largest sugar refinery, with a capacity of 2 million tonnes a year, and the largest oil refinery in Africa, producing 570,000 tonnes a year. It also produces vegetable fats, cereals, fruit-based beverages and mineral waters.

items.name: Biopharm
items.text: A pharmaceutical group listed on the Algiers stock exchange that makes medicines in Algeria, with a focus on cardiovascular and metabolic health and on contract manufacturing for other laboratories, at sites that meet European good manufacturing practice.

items.name: Yassir
items.text: Founded in Algeria in 2017, it brings ride-hailing, food delivery, grocery services and digital financial services into one app, with a network of drivers, merchants and delivery partners. It counts more than 8 million users across its markets.

items.name: Zergoun Green Energy
items.text: A private maker of solar modules whose plant in Ouargla was inaugurated with a capacity of 200 MW a year, on assembly lines from Spain’s Mondragon Assembly.

items.name: Mastrilo Academy
items.text: Founded by Oussama Djaidri and launched in 2024, an online platform that trains future professionals in digital skills and software development, with free and paid programmes.
